arxiv-2205-07589.title: Fundamental Laws of Binary Classification Thanks: Regularization methods presented in this paper appeared in WIREs Computational Statistics , 3: 204 - 215, 2011.
arxiv-2205-07589.creator: Denise M. Reeves
arxiv-2205-07589.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Denise M. Reeves. Finding discriminant functions of minimum risk binary classification systems is a novel geometric locus problem—which requires solving a system of fundamental locus equations of binary classification—subject to deep-seated statistical laws. arxiv-2209-08179.title: Cell Attention Networks
arxiv-2209-08179.creator: Lorenzo Giusti, Claudio Battiloro, Lucia Testa, Paolo Di Lorenzo, Stefania Sardellitti, Sergio Barbarossa
arxiv-2209-08179.description: Abstract Since their introduction, graph attention networks achieved outstanding results in graph representation learning tasks. However, these networks consider only pairwise relationships among nodes and then they are not able to fully exploit higher-order interactions present in many real world data-sets.

arxiv-2302-13814.title: An Independent Evaluation of ChatGPT on Mathematical Word Problems (MWP)
arxiv-2302-13814.creator: Paulo Shakarian, Abhinav Koyyalamudi, Noel Ngu, Lakshmivihari Mareedu
arxiv-2302-13814.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Paulo Shakarian, Abhinav Koyyalamudi, Noel Ngu, Lakshmivihari Mareedu. We study the performance of a commercially available large language model (LLM) known as ChatGPT on math word problems (MWPs) from the dataset DRAW-1K. To our knowledge, this is the first independent evaluation of ChatGPT. We found that ChatGPT’s performance changes dramatically based on the requirement to show its work, failing 20 % 20\% of the time when it provides work compared with 84 % 84\% when it does not.

arxiv-2305-01335.title: An Enigmatic 380 kpc Long Linear Collimated Galactic Tail 2023 An Enigmatic 380 kpc Long Linear Collimated Galactic Tail – References
arxiv-2305-01335.creator: Dennis Zaritsky Jacob P. Crossett, Yara L. Jaffé, Richard Donnerstein, Ananthan Karunakaran, Donghyeon J. Khim, Ana C.C. Lourenço, Kristine Spekkens, Ming Sun, Benedetta Vulcani
arxiv-2305-01335.description: Abstract We present an intriguing, serendipitously-detected system consisting of an S0/a galaxy, which we refer to as the “Kite", and a highly-collimated tail of gas and stars that extends over 380 kpc and contains pockets of star formation. In its length, narrowness, and linearity the Kite’s tail is an extreme example relative to known tails.

arxiv-2405-04748.title: On diagonal digraphs, Koszul algebras and triangulations of homology spheres
arxiv-2405-04748.creator: Sergei O. Ivanov, Lev Mukoseev
arxiv-2405-04748.description: Abstract . We study magnitude homology of digraphs, with a particular focus on diagonal digraphs, i.e., digraphs whose magnitude homology is concentrated on the diagonal. For any digraph G G , we provide a complete description of the second magnitude homology MH 2 , k ​ ( G ) \mathrm{MH}_{2,k}(G) .

arxiv-2501-11677.title: Squeezing generation crossing a mean-field critical point: Work statistics, irreversibility and critical fingerprints
arxiv-2501-11677.creator: Fernando J. Gómez-Ruiz, Stefano Gherardini, Ricardo Puebla
arxiv-2501-11677.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Fernando J. Gómez-Ruiz, Stefano Gherardini, Ricardo Puebla. Understanding the dynamical consequences of quantum phase transitions on thermodynamical quantities, such as work statistics and entropy production, is one of the most intriguing aspect of quantum many-body systems, pinpointing the emergence of irreversibility to critical features. In this work, we investigate the critical fingerprints appearing in these key thermodynamical quantities for a mean-field critical system undergoing a finite-time cycle, starting from a thermal state at a generic inverse temperature.

arxiv-2501-19314.title: An Efficient Approach for Machine Translation on Low-resource Languages: A Case Study in Vietnamese-Chinese
arxiv-2501-19314.creator: Tran Ngoc Son, Nguyen Anh Tu, Nguyen Minh TriSamsung SDS R&D Center, Hanoi, Vietnam {tn.son,na.tu,nm.tri}@gsamsung.com;
arxiv-2501-19314.description: Abstract Despite the rise of recent neural networks in machine translation, those networks do not work well if the training data is insufficient. In this paper, we proposed an approach for machine translation in low-resource languages such as Vietnamese-Chinese. Our proposed method leveraged the power of the multilingual pre-trained language model (mBART) and both Vietnamese and Chinese monolingual corpus.

arxiv-2601-13283.title: Surface Phonon Hall Viscosity Induced Phonon Chirality and Nonreciprocity in Magnetic Topological Insulator Films
arxiv-2601-13283.creator: Abhinava Chatterjee 1 , and Chao-Xing Liu ∗
arxiv-2601-13283.description: Abstract The surface half-quantum Hall effect, a hallmark consequence of axion electrodynamics, can be induced by gapping out the surface states of topological insulators through surface magnetization, and has led to a variety of topological response phenomena observed in experiments.

pmc-10507174.title: The organum vasculosum of the lamina terminalis and subfornical organ: regulation of thirst
pmc-10507174.creator: Jiaxu Wang, Fenglin Lv, Wei Yin, Zhanpeng Gao, Hongyu Liu, Zhen Wang, Jinhao Sun
pmc-10507174.description: Thirst and water intake are regulated by the organum vasculosum of the lamina terminalis (OVLT) and subfornical organ (SFO), located around the anteroventral third ventricle, which plays a critical role in sensing dynamic changes in sodium and water balance in body fluids.

pmc-10541965.title: Role of hypoxic exosomes and the mechanisms of exosome release in the CNS under hypoxic conditions
pmc-10541965.creator: Rong Yang, Zheng Li, Jing Xu, Juan Luo, Zhichuang Qu, Xin Chen, Sixun Yu, Haifeng Shu
pmc-10541965.description: Hypoxia is characterized by low oxygen levels in the body or environment, resulting in various physiological and pathological changes. The brain, which has the highest oxygen consumption of any organ, is particularly susceptible to hypoxic injury. Exposure to low-pressure hypoxic environments can cause irreversible brain damage.

pmc-10711522.title: DNA barcoding the ichthyofauna of the Beibu Gulf: Implications for fisheries management in a seafood market hub
pmc-10711522.creator: Changping Jiang, Murong Yi, Zhisen Luo, Xiongbo He, Hung‐Du Lin, Nicolas Hubert, Yunrong Yan
pmc-10711522.description: The Beibu Gulf in China is situated in the tropics, in the western Pacific Ocean. It is an emblematic region combining proximity to a marine biodiversity hotspot and a major seafood hub. Intensification of marine fishing and ocean warming led to a drastic decline in fish populations in the Beibu Gulf during the last decades.

pmc-11283479.title: Association between excessive alcohol consumption and incident diabetes mellitus among Japanese based on propensity score matching
pmc-11283479.creator: Changchun Cao, Cuimei Wei, Yong Han, Jiao Luo, Ping Xi, Jingying Chen, Xiaohua Xiao, Haofei Hu, Dongli Qi
pmc-11283479.description: The available evidence on the connection between excessive alcohol consumption and diabetes is controversial. Therefore, the primary objective of this investigation was to examine the connection between excessive alcohol consumption and incident diabetes in a Japanese population through the utilization of propensity score matching (PSM) analysis.

pmc-11311358.title: RNAseq of Gingival Fibroblasts Exposed to PRF Membrane Lysates and PRF Serum
pmc-11311358.creator: Atefe Imani, Layla Panahipour, Hannes Kühtreiber, Michael Mildner, Reinhard Gruber, Jelena Milasin, Miloš M Lazarević
pmc-11311358.description: Platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) is prepared by spontaneous coagulation of fractionated blood. When squeezed between two plates, PRF is separated into solid PRF membranes and a liquid exudate, the PRF serum. The question arises regarding how much the overall activity remains in the PRF membranes and what is discarded into the PRF serum.

pmc-11453410.title: 8007 The Effect of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists in Reducing Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis
pmc-11453410.creator: P H Romeiro, C R Silva, T T Mello, A Godoi, L C Hespanhol, C H Silva, C A Balieiro, H B Ferreira
pmc-11453410.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: The use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) is associated with a significant reduction in the incidence of major cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), suggesting a cardioprotective role for some drugs. However, which GLP-1RA is most effective at reducing MACE is unknown. Methods: PubMed, Embase and Cochrane Central databases were searched to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) that compared the safety of GLP-1RA with that of placebo in patients with T2DM.

pmc-11529104.title: Thyroid function tests in healthy kittens aged between 2 and 16 weeks
pmc-11529104.creator: Christina L Marino, Timothy A Bolton, Margret L Casal
pmc-11529104.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectivesThis study aimed to determine thyroid hormone concentrations in a cohort of healthy kittens due to the paucity of information in the literature, and the potential for congenital hypothyroidism (CH) to contribute to fading kitten syndrome (FKS).MethodsThe serum concentrations of total thyroxine (TT4), free thyroxine (fT4), total triiodothyronine (TT3), free triiodothyronine (fT3) and thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) were measured in 19 healthy kittens aged 2–16 weeks.ResultsMean TT4, fT4, TT3 and fT3 concentrations significantly differed across age groups.

pmc-12614872.title: The Impact of Lipaemia on the Laboratory Results in a Patient With Diabetes
pmc-12614872.creator: Quintin A van Staden, Minette Steyn, Anne-Cecilia van Marle, Jaco Joubert
pmc-12614872.description: Diabetic dyslipidaemia influences many laboratory results, which would not appear erroneous in the context of diabetic end organ damage, and can lead to inappropriate clinician response and treatment. Alternatively, abnormal results can be missed due to interference, again with potential consequences.

pmc-12631899.title: Substrate‐Controlled Response Coefficients in Thin Films
pmc-12631899.creator: Marina Tyunina, Leonid L Rusevich, Maxim Savinov, Tomas Kocourek, Oliva Pacherova, Alexandr Dejneka, Eugene A Kotomin
pmc-12631899.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). To obtain materials with desired properties, material compositions are primarily altered, whereas thin films offer additional unique avenues. By combining state‐of‐the‐art first‐principles calculations and experimental investigations of thin films of strontium titanate as an exemplary representative of a broad class of perovskite oxides and the extensive family of ferroelectrics, a novel approach is presented to achieving superior material responses to external stimuli. The findings reveal that substrate‐imposed deformations, or strains, significantly alter the frequencies and magnitudes of atomic vibrations in thin films.

pmc-13037120.title: Maternal age and the predictive performance of the uterine artery pulsatility index for composite adverse perinatal outcomes in late-onset fetal growth restriction: a retrospective cohort study
pmc-13037120.creator: Melisa Golgelioglu, Cigdem Akcabay, Gulcan Akverdi, Salih Burcin Kavak
pmc-13037120.description: BackgroundThis study aimed to evaluate whether the predictive performance of the uterine artery pulsatility index (UtA-PI) for composite adverse perinatal outcomes (CAPO) in late-onset fetal growth restriction (FGR) differs according to maternal age.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included singleton pregnancies with late-onset FGR (≥ 32 weeks of gestation) managed at a tertiary care center.

pmc-13239511.title: Elevated Nitrogen and Phosphorus Levels Suggest High Metabolic Demands in Himalayan High‐Elevation Plants
pmc-13239511.creator: Zuzana Chlumská, Martin Macek, Jan Altman, Michael Bartoš, Miroslav Dvorský, Martin Kopecký, Klára Řeháková, Lubomír Adamec, Jorge Gago, Kateřina Čapková, Jiří Doležal
pmc-13239511.description: Nutrient contents in plant tissues reflect adaptations and environmental constraints, varying across and within species along ecological gradients. Interspecific differences reflect long‐term adaptations, while intraspecific variations may indicate acclimation to present conditions. Examining these responses across elevational ranges is therefore crucial for understanding how nutrients influence species performance.

pmc-13317347.title: Absence of chlamydial infection in ocular adnexal MALT lymphoma based on next-generation sequencing
pmc-13317347.creator: Yoshihiro Yakushijin, Kazuhiro Horiba, Masanori Hashino, Shintaro Yamanaka, Shinji Hasebe, Shoichiro Yamamoto, Tomomi Fujii, Katsuto Takenaka, Masaki Yasukawa
pmc-13317347.description: ObjectivesExtranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) arises in various extranodal sites and has been linked to chronic inflammation, often triggered by infectious agents. Ocular adnexal (OA) MALT lymphoma has been associated with Chlamydophila psittaci (C. psittaci) in some regions. This study aimed to investigate the involvement of pathogenic microorganisms, including C. psittaci, in OA-MALT lymphoma.

pmc-13375497.title: Study on pathogenic bacteria distribution and antimicrobial resistance in adult urinary tract infections in a tertiary hospital in Southern Jiangxi, China, 2021–2024
pmc-13375497.creator: Zhengting Liu, Liqin Zhang, Cong Liu
pmc-13375497.description: BackgroundUrinary tract infections (UTIs) are common global bacterial infections. Rising antimicrobial resistance complicates their treatment. Analyzing pathogen distribution and resistance patterns in southern Jiangxi, China, is crucial for informing empirical treatment and infection management.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective study of 3,212 urinary isolates from adult UTI patients at our hospital from January 2021 to December 2024. We used WHONET 5.
